rejection_reasons: The extracted originals were hashed but not inserted into the compiled translation unit; probe.c independently rewrote tested algorithms.
The release control passed an asynchronous reply into the initial filter and discarded native copies instead of redispatching the INPUT_METHOD-flagged event.
Compilation and execution used the local workstation guard rather than the required remote dedicated-20cpu guard.
scope: Test-only source-bound model of the Mutter 50.1 input-method event dispatch and GTK 4.22.4 text-input-v3 commit/done consumer callbacks. Proves that the tested callback ordering permits commit overwrite before one deferred done and that an unfiltered release flushes pending done.
measured_facts: A legal run of three filtered press/release pairs and three IM_COMMIT events before the idle produces three Wayland commit strings, one done, and one GTK commit signal containing only the final string.
Running the deferred done after each commit produces three GTK commit signals and preserves abc.
Returning unfiltered for each release flushes the pending done before notify_key_event enqueues each native release copy; the model preserves abc and observes three native copies.
not_tested: Whether GNOME Text Editor used Mutter text-input-v3 for the captured failure
A live Mutter or GTK process, Wayland wire traffic, desktop pixels, physical input, or application state
Whether the captured cycle 9 followed the admissible coalesced schedule
Whether a release-only policy is portable across GTK IBus, X11, terminals, browsers, or other clients
Latency, RSS, package size, answer quality, and installed runtime behavior
verdict_scope: The callback chain admits the coalesced overwrite schedule. This is mechanism feasibility only, not live transport attribution or proof of the cycle 9 cause. Unfiltered release is a transport-specific scheduling lever, not an accepted repair.
